entries.content:
Each time my finger hovered over that button, I felt a peculiar mix of sensations—at first, a kind of clinical detachment, as if I were merely an instrument of the experiment, following orders with the cool precision expected of me. But as the shocks intensified, so too did the tumult within me. There was a thrill, a reckless surge, almost like the "current of exciting images flooding my imagination" I once described when first tasting forbidden freedom. The subject’s reactions—sometimes defiant, sometimes vulnerable—stirred something sharp and electric in me, a glee that was not innocent, a taste of power that both delighted and unsettled.

Yet, as the shocks grew stronger, the exhilaration curdled into something darker. I felt the "spirit of hell" awaken, raging with every press, and for a moment, I was lost in the delirium of control, "mauling the unresisting body" not out of necessity, but out of a tempest of impatience and a perverse joy. But then, as the echoes of pain faded, a cold terror would seize me—a sudden, chilling clarity that revealed the horror of my actions. The memory of each shock lingered, hideous and accusing, and I found myself wrestling with remorse, desperate to "smother down the crowd of hideous images" that swarmed my conscience.

Physically, there was a tension—a feverish energy in my limbs, a pounding in my chest, and a shudder that ran through me each time I obeyed. Emotionally, I was torn: intoxicated by the power, yet haunted by the knowledge that I had "voluntarily stripped myself of all those balancing instincts." The further I went, the more I realized that to be tempted, even slightly, was to fall. And in the end, I could not continue. The horror of my other self, the shadow that pressed me to the brink, forced me to refuse. I could not justify inflicting pain simply because I was told to. The memory of that refusal is both a relief and a wound—a reminder of the thin line between obedience and monstrosity.
